evidence: View A: Four remembered items — upper is a green triangle
the right/yellow square is least recoverable
the lower/blue cross and the upper/green triangle have higher predicted recoverability if not attended next
The system is currently attending the left/red circle, so that item is most immediately available.

Predicted effects of commands are strong and specific: issuing a command toward a given A location overwhelmingly moves selection to that location, so attention in A is under effective control and can be redirected to any single item.
View B: Four remembered items — upper is a yellow square
the right/blue triangle also has relatively high recoverability if accessed
lower is a mostly green cross
The system is currently attending the lower/green cross, making it the most immediately available now

predicted next selections are biased toward the left location under most commands, so attempts to redirect attention in B are likely to shift selection to the left/red circle rather than reliably to arbitrary targets. Thus A is readily controllable; B is biased toward left.
